answer.rationale: c4 confirms the incumbent has moved on price when challenged with market data before; c6 confirms longer commitments have unlocked volume pricing without scope narrowing. Together they support going back to the incumbent with a market benchmark AND a multi-year structure, even after their initial refusal — finance needs 18% off, and the lever that previously worked was benchmarking, not switching. Switching now (c2/c3 logic) would risk the 94%-utilization line with onboarding/integration variance. Renewing outright (c1) misses the mandate. Deferring (c5) preserves flexibility but doesn't cut spend and the contract does not auto-renew — deferral effectively means going month-to-month at current price, which fails the cost objective. Adding a second source (c3) is a resilience lever, not a cost lever this cycle. So: return to the incumbent with a benchmarked, multi-year offer structured to hit the 18% target; if they refuse again, switch becomes the next-cycle move.
